title: Spatial and Temporal Locators
lede: Move beyond simple “in” and “to”. Describe where objects and landmarks are in relation to one another, and place events before, after or during another time.

items.prompt: The school is in front of the mosque.
items.feedback: أَمَامَ creates a relation between two places.
تَحْتَ means below or under.

items.prompt: Choose “between the bank and the shop”.
items.feedback: Both coordinated nouns belong to the locator phrase.

items.prompt: Which is best for “during the lesson”?
items.feedback: أَثْنَاءَ places an action within an event.

items.prompt: Many words such as أَمَامَ and خَلْفَ are technically…
options: locative nouns/adverbs used in an iḍāfa-like phrase
items.feedback: Cambridge groups them functionally with prepositions, but the following noun is a genitive complement.
بِجَانِبِ means beside or next to.

items.prompt: The picture is above the sofa.
items.feedback: فَوْقَ expresses the higher position.

items.prompt: The garden is behind the house.
items.feedback: خَلْفَ expresses behind.

items.prompt: The pharmacy is opposite the hospital.
items.feedback: مُقَابِلَ expresses facing/opposite.
بالقرب من means near.
Both coordinated nouns are in the locator phrase.
The dual complement uses ـَيْنِ.

options: at / by / with, according to context
items.feedback: عند is a flexible high-frequency locator.
عند locates something at/by a point.
After in time is بَعْدَ.

items.prompt: Do not talk during the exam.
items.feedback: أثناء locates an action within an event.

items.prompt: I have lived here for two years / since two years ago.
items.feedback: منذ marks the starting point or elapsed period.
قبل + genitive time phrase.
أمام = in front of.
مقابل = opposite.
Dual genitive complement uses ـَيْنِ.
Beside = بجانب + genitive/possessive noun.
خلال expresses during/throughout.
بعد is temporal.
The fixed phrase is بالقرب من.

Functional use is the examination priority.

blocks: ## Why this matters
Precise locator phrases turn a vague description into usable directions and a clear picture of a room, town or journey.
### Core
Use front, behind, above, below and beside.
### Develop
Describe maps using between, opposite, near and far.
### Stretch
Distinguish technical locator nouns from true particle prepositions.
[callout] Communication target: Give a stranger enough information to locate a building without seeing your map.
## Diagnostic start
Identify the relationship before concentrating on endings.
## The spatial locator system
Most spatial locators come before a noun that completes their meaning.

TABLE: Locator | Meaning | Model // أَمَامَ | in front of | السَّيَّارَةُ أَمَامَ الْبَيْتِ. // وَرَاءَ | behind / beyond | الْحَدِيقَةُ وَرَاءَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ. // خَلْفَ | behind | الْمَوْقِفُ خَلْفَ الْمَتْجَرِ. // فَوْقَ | above / over | الصُّورَةُ فَوْقَ السَّرِيرِ. // تَحْتَ | under / below | الْحَقِيبَةُ تَحْتَ الْكُرْسِيِّ. // بِجَانِبِ | beside / next to | الْمَكْتَبَةُ بِجَانِبِ الْمَسْجِدِ. // مُقَابِلَ | opposite / facing | الْمَطْعَمُ مُقَابِلَ الْفُنْدُقِ. // قُرْبَ / بِالْقُرْبِ مِنْ | near | أَسْكُنُ بِالْقُرْبِ مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ. // بَعِيدًا عَنْ | far from | الْمَطَارُ بَعِيدٌ عَنِ الْمَدِينَةِ. // حَوْلَ | around | تُوجَدُ أَشْجَارٌ حَوْلَ الْبَيْتِ. // دَاخِلَ | inside | الطُّلَّابُ دَاخِلَ الْفَصْلِ. // خَارِجَ | outside | الْحَافِلَةُ خَارِجَ الْمَحَطَّةِ.

[callout] Technical accuracy without overload: Words such as أَمَامَ، خَلْفَ، فَوْقَ are often analysed as locative nouns/adverbs rather than particle prepositions. Functionally, learn the complete pattern: locator + genitive noun.
## Between, with and two-part relations
Some locators require attention to more than one noun.
[ar] الْمَكْتَبَةُ بَيْنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ وَالْمَسْجِدِ.
[ar] جَلَسْتُ بَيْنَ صَدِيقَيْنِ.
[ar] ذَهَبْتُ مَعَ أَخِي وَأُخْتِي.
[ar] الْمَتْجَرُ عِنْدَ نِهَايَةِ الشَّارِعِ.
[callout/warning] Between two places: In بَيْنَ الْبَنْكِ وَالْمَتْجَرِ , both nouns belong to the coordinated relationship. Do not change the second noun back to nominative merely because of وَ .
## Locators of time
The same architecture can locate an action in relation to another time or event.

TABLE: Time locator | Meaning | Model // قَبْلَ | before | أَسْتَيْقِظُ قَبْلَ السَّابِعَةِ. // بَعْدَ | after | أَدْرُسُ بَعْدَ الْغَدَاءِ. // أَثْنَاءَ | during | لَا أَسْتَعْمِلُ هَاتِفِي أَثْنَاءَ الدَّرْسِ. // خِلَالَ | during / throughout | تَعَلَّمْتُ كَثِيرًا خِلَالَ الْعُطْلَةِ. // مُنْذُ | since / for from a starting point | أَسْكُنُ هُنَا مُنْذُ سَنَتَيْنِ. // حَتَّى | until | أَدْرُسُ حَتَّى السَّاعَةِ الثَّامِنَةِ.
[callout] Boundary for later lessons: قَبْلَ أَنْ , بَعْدَ أَنْ and مُنْذُ أَنْ link clauses and appear again in Lesson 5.
## From map to connected description
A good description combines a reference point, a precise relation and a route.
[ar] يَقَعُ الْبَنْكُ مُقَابِلَ الْمَكْتَبَةِ، وَالْمَقْهَى بِجَانِبِهِ.
[ar] سِرْ إِلَى نِهَايَةِ الشَّارِعِ، ثُمَّ اِنْعَطِفْ يَمِينًا عِنْدَ الْمَسْجِدِ.
[callout] Reading strategy: Draw a quick sketch while reading directions. Spatial words often carry more information than unfamiliar descriptive vocabulary.
## Misconception and proofreading clinic
Correct the relationship, not only the ending.

TABLE: Incorrect | Correct | Repair // الْمَطْعَمُ أَمَامُ الْفُنْدُقُ. | الْمَطْعَمُ أَمَامَ الْفُنْدُقِ. | locator form + genitive complement // الْبَنْكُ بَيْنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ وَالْمَتْجَرُ. | الْبَنْكُ بَيْنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ وَالْمَتْجَرِ. | second coordinated noun remains in the relation // أَدْرُسُ خَلْفَ الْغَدَاءِ. | أَدْرُسُ بَعْدَ الْغَدَاءِ. | use a temporal, not spatial, locator // الْمَطَارُ بِالْقُرْبِ عَنِ الْمَدِينَةِ. | الْمَطَارُ بِالْقُرْبِ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ. | fixed phrase بالقرب من
## Grammar game
Read each clue and select the locator that represents the relationship.
## Skills workshop التَّطْبِيقُ الْعَمَلِيُّ
Use a plan, map and timetable to communicate location and sequence.
[ar] فِي غُرْفَتِي سَرِيرٌ بِجَانِبِ النَّافِذَةِ، وَمَكْتَبٌ مُقَابِلَ الْبَابِ.
[ar] الْمَدْرَسَةُ بَيْنَ الْمَسْجِدِ وَالْمَكْتَبَةِ، وَمَوْقِفُ الْحَافِلَاتِ أَمَامَهَا.
### Describe a room or local map
Write 70–90 Arabic words describing the position of at least six objects or landmarks and explaining one short route.
[callout] Success checklist: Use six spatial locators; include one بَيْنَ phrase with two nouns; include one time locator; use a connector to sequence the route.
[callout] Paper route: Draw the room or map first. Label it in Arabic, then write a connected description beneath it.
## Final mastery check
Check spatial meaning, genitive forms and time relationships.
### What you can now do
- Build locator + genitive noun phrases.
- Describe objects and landmarks with precise spatial relationships.
- Use بَيْنَ with two coordinated genitive nouns.
- Place actions in time with قَبْلَ، بَعْدَ، أَثْنَاءَ and خِلَالَ.
Spaced revisit: Return in two or three days and complete the final check again without looking at the tables.
